newsitem.title: USA: Lott says Clinton may have to sign tax bill first.
newsitem.headline: Lott says Clinton may have to sign tax bill first.

text.p: If President Clinton threatens to veto a tax bill because it does not meet his specifications, Republicans may hold off on sending him the spending portion of budget legislation, Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Wednesday.

"He (Clinton) thinks we're going to send him the spending increases that he wants and then allow him to veto a tax bill? What kind of good faith is that?" Lott, a Mississippi Republican, told the National Retail Federation.

"We may not send him a spending bill until he signs a tax bill...we're not going to give him an opportunity to knock out the part we really care about and get the part he really cares about," Lott said.
Congressional leaders and the White House agreed Friday to a broad outline of a budget aimed at wiping out the deficit by 2002. It included $85 billion net tax cuts over five years.
The tax package is expected to include capital gains and estate tax relief, a child credit and tuition credit.
